title: Chapter 11 — The Second Price
description: Abundance needs new branches. Chief Ọ̀dụ̀ asks for one hungry boy, and Kalu, Ngozi's apprentice, is very hungry.

beats.speaker: chiefOdu
beats.text: Brother. Abundance grows like a tree. Every branch must grow a branch. Bring us one hungry boy before the new moon.

variants.text: Brother. You counted your blessing on the floor, in front of Ike. The book noticed. Now it wants a branch: one hungry boy, before the new moon.

beats.speaker: usher
beats.text: (waiting at the Back Side, very polite) You said no to the white chair. The Chief has decided to be generous. Bring us one hungry boy, and your "no" will be forgotten.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You know exactly which boy. Everyone at Ọjà knows Kalu: seventeen, Ngozi's apprentice, sharp as a broken bottle, and in love with every Benz that drives past.

beats.speaker: kalu
beats.text: Oga Emeka! (He calls you Oga now. Nobody else does.) I hear say you dey go Island parties. Carry me one day. I fit wear white, I fit wear anything.

beats.speaker: kalu
beats.text: Madam Ngozi says you are the only honest Igbo man at Ọjà. (He grins.) She also says it is a disease.

beats.speaker: kalu
beats.text: He is looking at you the way you looked at Ike's Benz.

options.text: "There is a party. White attire. I'll take you."
"Kalu. If a man in white ever invites you anywhere, run. Promise me."
Say nothing. Buy him a Fanta and leave.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Night of Increase. Kalu in white, borrowed from you, too big at the shoulders. He signs fast. He doesn't ask anything. You didn't either.

beats.speaker: chiefOdu
beats.text: (handing you a pair of white gloves) Ushers wear these. You have the gift, brother. People trust your face. Stay with us. Bring more.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You are good at it. That is the worst part. Market boys, bus conductors, a nurse, a footballer. They trust your face. You bring them to the white chair and hold the door.

beats.title: The Usher
beats.summary: You stopped being the hungry one and became the one who finds them. The gloves never get dirty.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: No boy for the Chief. The new moon comes. So do the ushers, under the bridge, on your way home.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Three of them. White cars at both ends of the road.

options.text: Take Prof's back way through the market. They don't know it.
options.lockedText: You never learned the back ways

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Under the danfo, through Mama Put's kitchen, over the wall behind the motor park. Prof's routes. The white cars wait at both ends of an empty road for an hour.

won.toast: Two ushers on the ground in white. White shows dirt very well.

lost.toast: They don't hit your face. They never hit faces. They take your wallet and your sleep.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: When you get home, the floor where Uncle Dozie slept is empty. So is the tin under the mattress. A note: "Nephew. Lagos is too big. I took transport. Forgive. —D." He took ₦30,000 in "transport".

beats.speaker: nneEmeka
beats.text: (a voice note) Dozie came home. He sat in my kitchen and told me about Papa and the man in white. Then he cried and ate all my fish. (A pause.) Thank you for sending him.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You listen to Dozie's recording again, at 2 a.m. "Your father died saying no." You save it in three places.

beats.title: The Second Price
beats.summary: The book wanted a branch. You either gave it Kalu, or you gave it a fight. Either way, the Fellowship has written your name a second time.
